newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares began the day firmer and staged a further strong advance after positively received U.S. labour market data.
The AEX index of 25 blue chips finished up 18 points or over two percent at a new closing high of 897.10 after briefly breaking through 900 for the first time just before the close.
This brings the AEX's rise to 38 percent since the end of 1996 and to 60 percent over the last 12 months.
Dealers said there seemed to be no reason for sentiment to turn sour but noted that retail investors were driving the rally while professionals were turning increasingly cautious.

"Some fund managers are getting quite worried at how sharply the market has risen and are adjusting their portfolios to track the index more. So if prices start to fall, at least they won't do worse than the market as a whole," said one dealer.
The same dealer said this largely explained the gains posted by index heavyweights such as Royal Dutch Petroleum, up 4.20 at 112.20 and Unilever, up 11.40 at 442.30.

Heineken stood out among blue chips with a loss of four guilders at 348.50. Some dealers cited worries that poor summer weather in Europe could produce a second consecutive year of disappointing earnings for the brewer in 1997.

Despite the ease with which the AEX has taken out the 700, 800 and 900 markers so far this year, some dealers said the rally seemed set to roll on indefinitely as a growing number of Europeans shunned low bond yields and turned to the stock market in the hope of securing a healthy retirement income.
